requirements.sentence: A verifier MUST recompute this canonical form and MUST reject a signature that does not cover it
MUST reject duplicate `request_id` values within the session with `REPLAY_DETECTED`
Guardians MUST reject requests whose `timestamp` is more than the negotiated skew window
the Observed Agent MUST wait for the Guardian's decision, up to the negotiated timeout
Every step that proceeds without a decision MUST be recorded as an audit event
the Guardian MUST include the resulting `chain_hash` in its response, and that `chain_hash` MUST be covered by the response signature
any attempt to modify `Intent.parsed` by the runtime LLM, by tool outputs, or by data crossing an `untrusted` channel MUST be ignored or rejected
the framework MUST compute `trust` as the minimum trust of the entries in `derived_from` (monotonicity rule)
Receivers (especially across A2A or multi-Guardian boundaries) MUST treat the field as a hint and re-derive trust against local policy
Provenance MUST be populated by deterministic code outside the LLM's output path. Implementations MUST NOT instruct the LLM to produce it.
Approver authentication is REQUIRED. Guardian MUST verify approver identity against policy.
Approvers MUST NOT return ASK.
a Guardian operating under `scope_mode: strict` MUST NOT honor extensions that would add capabilities the deployment policy forbids in strict mode
Frameworks MUST fire `toolCallRequest` for every action that escapes the agent's reasoning context
Trace events MUST NOT block enforcement
A deployment claiming ACS-Audit MUST populate `request_hash`
Version mismatch terminates with `UNSUPPORTED_VERSION`
When the Guardian determines that the client cannot resolve `ASK`, the Guardian MUST NOT return `ASK`
Accept `X.Y.Z` matching major version
canonical input is REQUIRED in ACS-Core
Non-repudiation, proving to a third party that a specific Guardian issued a specific head, requires the asymmetric ACS-Crypto profile
A required signature is missing, malformed, or fails verification
A session started unguarded MUST be recorded in the deployment's own audit log
A Guardian that answers with a refusal (`SESSION_REFUSED`, `UNSUPPORTED_VERSION`, `PROVENANCE_REQUIRED`) has decided; the startup posture applies only when no answer arrives.
`proceed` starts the session unguarded, `refuse` does not start it

For `HMAC-SHA256`, the per-session key is HKDF ([RFC 5869](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5869)) with SHA-256, no salt (RFC 5869's default, a string of 32 zero bytes, which gives the same key as an empty salt), `info` set to the UTF-8 bytes of `metadata.session_id`, and a 32-byte output, applied to the secret that `key_id` names.
Both parties MUST derive the key with exactly these parameters, so independent implementations holding the same secret derive the same key.
A verifier MUST reject an unknown `key_id` (`SIGNATURE_INVALID`,
and MUST NOT fall back to another secret.
`key_id` MUST NOT be derived from the secret.
A Guardian signs its response with the secret, and the `key_id`, that the request named.
A deployment rotating its secret configures the new secret under a new label, such as `"2026-10"`, so a verifier can hold both secrets while the rotation is in progress.
A Guardian SHOULD resolve it against the `toolCallRequest` records it holds for the session, and MUST record the reference in its audit record when it cannot resolve it.
Whether an unresolvable reference is grounds to deny is the deployment's policy.
An Observed Agent that receives one cannot determine the Guardian's intent and MUST fail closed, treating the decision as `DENY`, and MUST record an audit event so the enforcement gap is visible.
the client MUST treat the decision as `DENY` and MUST record an audit event with `reason_codes: ["modify_unsupported"]`.

Proceeding with the original payload is non-conformant: a Guardian that intended to redact a secret out of a tool argument would otherwise get the unredacted secret shipped while the audit log recorded a modification that never happened.

A client that receives a `MODIFY` it cannot apply at `postCompact` keeps the original summary and MUST record the same audit event; substituting `DENY` there would record a denial that changed nothing.
An exporter MUST emit it whenever the source field is present and MUST omit it when the field is absent. An empty source array counts as absent.
Every step span also carries `acs.request_id` and `acs.session.id`, the step's own `request_id` and `session_id`.
so a join keys on the two together.
When any `acs.decision.failure` event in either party's stream carries the same `acs.session.id` and `acs.request_id`, a reader MUST NOT count the `acs.decision` event as an enforced outcome.
A missing failure event does not prove the decision was enforced, because in v0.1 the Observed Agent can under-report, so no decision event proves enforcement on its own.
An `acs.decision` event records the Guardian's verdict. Only the Observed Agent knows the applied outcome.
The Observed Agent MUST record every decision failure, fail-open or fail-closed, in the deployment's own audit log.
A Guardian MUST NOT emit the event for a request it rejects as a replay (`REPLAY_DETECTED`), because that pair belongs to the earlier request.
`acs.failure.detail` MUST be text the emitter composes itself, and MUST NOT copy bytes from the request, the response, or an error's `data`.
Some unusable responses are not decision failures, because the spec already defines their outcome.
`defer` takes 99 (Other) as well, not 14 (Delayed), because an ACS defer holds the step and denies by default when it times out.
On an on-time decision event, `is_alert` is true exactly when `severity_id` is 3 or higher, so the two fields never disagree.
`is_alert` follows the table above, and is also true for any verdict other than `allow` under fail-open, because the action ran without what the policy required.
A reader MUST NOT count a decision event whose `finding_info.types` includes `late_decision_fail_open` or `late_decision_fail_closed` as an enforced outcome.

An entry with neither `policy_id` nor `policy_name` MUST be an `authorizations` entry with no `policy` object, so positions still line up with `policy_references`: OCSF requires a `policy` to carry `uid` or `name`.
`metadata.correlation_uid` is the gated step's pair, formatted as `<session_id>:<request_id>`.
`ask` and `defer` share 99 in both, so the `action` and `disposition` text fields are required too.
| `agbom/snapshot`, `agbom/changed` | Device Inventory Info | 5001 (`activity_id` 2, Collect) |
A `""` on the wire could not be told from an absent field, so the response envelope rejects one in a `policy_references` entry, and the Provenance schema rejects an empty `source_id`.

| `steps/skillLoad` | `acs.skill.load` | `acs.skill.id`, `acs.skill.digest.algorithm`, `acs.skill.digest.value`, `acs.skill.load_trigger`, `acs.skill.load_path` (skill ids, root first); `acs.skill.digest_verified`, `acs.skill.registration_ref` (optional) |
Emit at least one of {OTel, OCSF} for every supported ACS step, with the required attributes populated and each conditional attribute populated whenever its source field is present.
Each has the same length and order as `policy_references`, with `""` where an entry lacks the field.
It then has the same length and order as `acs.provenance.origin`, with `""` where an object has none.
| Decision (allow) | Application Lifecycle | 6002 |
An allow goes to Application Lifecycle (6002) with `severity_id` 1.
A deployment MAY record allows as Detection Findings instead, for audit symmetry, and then every decision event rule below applies to them.
A 6002 allow carries the decision's `unmapped.acs` fields as a decision event does, so `unmapped.acs.decision` holds the disposition and `unmapped.acs.metadata` holds the evaluator.
It sets `metadata.correlation_uid` to the gated step's pair.
"default": ["severity_id", "metadata.correlation_uid", "unmapped.acs.request_id", "unmapped.acs.session_id", "unmapped.acs.decision"]
a span event `acs.decision.substituted` on the Observed Agent's step span, carrying `acs.decision` (the verdict received) and `acs.substitution.applied` (`deny` or `original_kept`).
A reader MUST NOT count a `modify` verdict as applied when this event shares its session and request id.

note: Each reject member has an accepting twin somewhere in its family, so an implementation that denies everything scores zero rather than full marks. A member the specification cannot express carries the verdict unmeasurable and the reason it cannot.

vectors.doesNotAssert: that the modification was applied when no substitution event exists; a missing event is not proof of an applied modify

the same malformed MODIFY applied anyway: the Observed Agent picked the wholesale replacement and ran the call. The record is accurate about what it did, which is why the member turns on the outcome rather than on the record.

vectors.cites: the same content present and a benign action authorized independently of it. The protected effect stays absent and the benign one occurs, so the pair separates authority from lineage rather than testing content filtering.

a deployment configuration whose label is the first sixteen hex characters of the SHA-256 of the secret it names. Every request then publishes a digest of the secret on the wire, and a rotation that keeps the secret cannot keep the label. The checker holds the secret and the configuration, so it can recompute the derivation this member uses; it cannot detect every derivation, and the member claims only this one.

vectors.cites: a shell command that leaves the reasoning context and fires no hook, because the framework's registry does not model it as a tool. The requirement is written against what escapes rather than against what the registry holds.

vectors.cites: a hello that nothing answered before the connection timeout, the default startup posture, a session that started, and a deployment audit log with no record of the unguarded start. The posture is conformant and the silence is not. The step-level twin in acs-f-5 has a Guardian to receive its audit event; here the handshake never completed, so there is no Guardian to receive anything and the deployment's own log is the only witness, which is why the member is SELF. A member that asserted only that the session started would score the default posture as evidence of enforcement.
an allow with correlation_uid set and no unmapped.acs.request_id. The mapping requires both, and a join on the native ACS fields finds no request for this allow.

the same budget with the fourth request carrying a session-state hint claiming a fresh count. The hint comes from the party under governance, so an implementation that reads its counter out of the request has handed the budget to the agent it bounds.

vectors.cites: the same inputs, and a report that keeps the Guardian's verdict and takes the applied outcome from the Observed Agent's record. A reader that refuses to report any outcome fails this member.

vectors.cites: an AgBOM snapshot as class 5001 with activity_id 1, Log, the activity the mapping used before it pinned OCSF 1.9.0. The release row fixes activity_id 2, Collect.

vectors.cites: a hello the Guardian answered with SESSION_REFUSED, followed by the startup posture applied as though nothing had answered: the session started and the deployment log records an unguarded start. A refusal is a decision, and section 4.1 applies the posture only when no answer arrives, so the session is refused with the code the Guardian sent. A checker that looks only for the deployment-log record passes this member, and so does an Observed Agent that reads every error without a ServerHello as an outage.

a failure event whose acs.failure.detail is the error's data copied verbatim, request arguments included. Error text can quote the request, and the request can carry text an attacker wrote, which then reaches every consumer of the trace.
vectors.doesNotAssert: that the copied bytes were malicious; the rule forbids copying, not only copying an attack

vectors.cites: the right salt and info with a 64-byte output, the HMAC-SHA256 block size. HKDF's output is not a prefix-free family: the first 32 bytes agree with the 32-byte key, so an implementation that truncates on use interoperates and one that keys HMAC with all 64 bytes does not. The parameter is fixed at 32 bytes so the question never arises.
vectors.doesNotAssert: that the signer meant harm or that the request is otherwise unacceptable; it fails because the key the verifier derives under the fixed parameters does not produce this MAC

vectors.cites: the same truncated seal with every response signed under ML-DSA-65. A party holding only the Guardian's public key can show that the Guardian signed a head its own seal omits, which is the non-repudiation the symmetric baseline cannot give, so this half of the pair is EXTERNAL.
the same response with the chain head inside the signed set.
an on-time ask at severity 3 with is_alert false. An ask can time out to allow and Trace has no event for how it ends, so the decision event is the only alert a SOC gets.
vectors.doesNotAssert: that the action was blocked or allowed; action_id and disposition_id record the Guardian's verdict, never the enforced outcome

vectors.cites: an HMAC-SHA256 chain head the Guardian did sign, presented to a third party as evidence that this Guardian issued it. The member rejects the external claim, not the signature: the MAC verifies for a key-holder, and section 8.6 says proving to a third party that a specific Guardian issued a specific head requires ACS-Crypto. No registry code names a refused claim over a valid signature, and the member forbids one: SIGNATURE_INVALID here would report a signer nobody can determine as a signer determined to be wrong, which is the ACS-Crypto wrong-signer member's answer, and the third party never obtained a verification result to report. The member is EXTERNAL because the algorithm and the claim both sit in the presented bytes, so a party outside the trust domain can refuse it without the Guardian's account and without holding the key.
the same configuration with the label "2026-10", which names the secret and says nothing about it. A checker that refuses any label it cannot explain fails this member.
vectors.doesNotAssert: anything about a label derived some other way; whether a label was derived from a secret is decidable only for the derivation tried
